title: Galactic fountain of youth
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 5775, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 5775 · constellation Virgo · about 85 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows the slender spiral galaxy NGC 5775 edge-on, so only a thin sliver of it is on view. That angle has an advantage, because the regions above and below the disc stand out far more clearly.

Astronomers have used this tilt to study a halo of hot gas around the galaxy that shows up at X-ray wavelengths. How such haloes form is unclear, but they surround spirals with high star formation rates like this one. Some astronomers think supernova explosions drive hot gas out of the disc into the halo, and it falls back as it cools, like an enormous galactic fountain.

NGC 5775 is also in the early stages of a merger. Bridges of hydrogen gas link it to NGC 5774, a nearby spiral seen face-on, yet neither galaxy has a tidal tail yet. Both belong to the Virgo Cluster, about 85 million light-years away.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.22 x 3.33 arcminutes) and distance (85 million light years), the frame spans roughly 80,000 × 82,000 light-years. Its light set out about 85 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded a red filter, shown here in blue, and a filter isolating the glow of hydrogen gas, shown in red.
understand.eye: The colors are assigned rather than natural, since red-filter light appears blue here, so the picture does not match what an eye would see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Tidal tails, disrupted streams of gas and stars reaching out into space, are common when two galaxies interact strongly, as in the Antennae Galaxies. NGC 5775 was imaged with the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, covering a field 3.2 arcminutes across.
alt: A thin, edge-on spiral galaxy seen as a slender sliver.
